title: BBQ Fillet Steak
summary: A thick fillet seared over the hottest part of the BBQ with the lid down, then finished on the cooler side to a pink medium-rare.

steps.heading: Before you start
steps.text: Take the steak out of the fridge {timer:45} before cooking. Pat it very dry and salt it generously on all sides. Keep the pepper for after cooking.

Preheat the BBQ with the lid closed for {timer:15}. You want the hot side as hot as it goes, around {temp:280-300}, and the other side much gentler. On a BBQ with a grill and a carbon plate, the grill is the hot side and the plate the cooler one.
Clean the grill and oil it lightly.

steps.heading: Cook
steps.text: Put the fillet on the hot grill, close the lid and cook for {timer:2.5} without touching it.
Open the lid and turn the steak 90° on the same side, for crosshatch marks. Close the lid and cook for another {timer:2.5}.
Open the lid, turn the steak over, close the lid and cook for {timer:2.5}.
Open the lid, turn it 90° again, close the lid and cook for {timer:2}.
Move the fillet to the cooler side and close the lid.

Check it with the thermometer, pushed into the centre from the side. At {temp:48-49!}, leave it on the cooler side with the lid closed for another minute. At {temp:50-52!}, or above, take it off straight away.

steps.heading: Rest and serve
steps.text: Rest it for {timer:7-8|rest}, unwrapped; tent it loosely with foil only if it is windy.
Serve it whole or sliced into medallions, with a little flaky salt and black pepper if you like.

tips: Trust the thermometer over the clock. After resting it finishes at 54-56 °C, a pink medium-rare.
Use tongs, never a fork, and never press the steak down.
Cooking it with the A5 Wagyu: the Wagyu goes on the hot grill at the moment the fillet moves to the cooler side, and both are ready to eat at about the same time.
